topQuotes.author: timbo415
topQuotes.text: Theory I have: it's often the temperature of the wine. Too often at home people are drinking reds at room temp rather than trying to get them to ~57°F before drinking.
topQuotes.thread: Why does wine taste better at the winery?

topQuotes.author: NapoleonTrilobite
topQuotes.text: Wineries invest a lot of time and money into immersive tasting experiences. They guide you through tasting notes while you're at a beautiful venue and having great conversation with wines that have properly breathed in pristine stemware. There are so many itty bitty factors contributing to you drinking that first glass.
topQuotes.thread: Why does wine taste better at the winery?

topQuotes.author: Jealous-Breakfast-86
topQuotes.text: I used to drink almost entirely reds. At the moment, I likely drink way more whites. I used to seek out the most intense fruit bombs I could find. Now I like funky flavours and subtlety as well.
topQuotes.thread: How have your opinions on wine changed?

topQuotes.author: DumbassPhysicist
topQuotes.text: Ameztoi Txakolina or the Ameztoi Rubentis Rosé. Both with a good chill kept me alive in the hot and humid summers of Boston.

topQuotes.author: NWisthebest
topQuotes.text: For the most part it will be based on my seasonal cooking habits. In summer I eat more salad and grill more. In winter I do more roasting and braising. Therefore I find myself drinking crisp whites in summer, whereas in winter I lean towards richer whites and more complex reds. Of course, when it all comes down to it, I drink whatever the hell I want, whenever the hell I want!
topQuotes.thread: Which wines do you associate with the seasons?

topQuotes.author: blondybee
topQuotes.text: Summer: Rosé or Gruner. Fall: Zweigelt. Winter: Zin, Cab or Barolo. Spring: Sauv Blanc or Gruner again lol.
topQuotes.thread: Which wines do you associate with the seasons?

topQuotes.author: WhiskeyandCigars7
topQuotes.text: Giuseppe Attanasio Primitivo di Manduria. Clocking in at 16.5%. Chocolate, baked cherries, fertile black soil, figs. Viscous and intense flavors. Pairs great with a fireplace or bonfire, blankets, and good company.
topQuotes.thread: Best wine for a cold winter night?

topQuotes.author: ThatFrenchieGuy

topQuotes.thread: Which wines do you associate with the seasons?
